An attacker does not require authentication or access to the `/status` endpoint in order to trigger XSS, but may simply visit a URI embedding the malicious code. 1. Navigate to `example.com/` 2. Navigate to `example.com/status?full&html` 3. Observe the JavaScript pop-up. The same is possible for the XML endpoint, possibly embedding malicious XML nodes into the status report. 1. Navigate to `example.com/<` 2. Navigate to `example.com/status?full&xml` 3. Scope: More severe when a scope change occurs, e.g. one vulnerable component impacts resources in components beyond its security scope. # Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via TrafficShaper description in legacy PHP firewall rules page High fichtner published GHSA-m4m3-v627-wgc2 Jun 15, 2026 ## Package opnsense/core ## Affected versions <= 26.1.9, <= 26.4 ## Patched versions 26.1.10, 26.4.1 ## Description #### Summary A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability allows an authenticated administrator to inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the browser of any other administrator who opens the Firewall Rules edit page. The attack vector passes through the MVC framework's TrafficShaper model — whose `description` field accepts arbitrary characters including HTML tags — and triggers in a legacy PHP page that outputs stored values without HTML escaping. #### Details The vulnerability spans two OPNsense subsystems: Input side (MVC framework): The TrafficShaper model (`src/opnsense/mvc/app/models/OPNsense/TrafficShaper/TrafficShaper.php`) defines the `description` field as a `DescriptionField`. The validation regex is `/^(.){1,255}$/`, which permits arbitrary characters including `<`, `>`, `"`, and `'`. Payloads are stored in the OPNsense config XML without sanitization. Data flow: `firewall_rules_edit.php:44` loads all shaper targets via the model: $shaper_targets = (new \OPNsense\TrafficShaper\TrafficShaper())->fetchAllTargets(); The traffic shaper pipe objects — including the attacker-controlled `description` field — are passed to the template and rendered in a shaper dropdown at lines 1400 and 1412. Sink (legacy PHP): `src/www/firewall_rules_edit.php` at lines 1400 and 1412: No `htmlspecialchars()` or any other escaping is applied. The MVC framework's global JSON escaping in `Response.php:121` (`htmlspecialchars($json, ENT_NOQUOTES)`) only protects API JSON responses and does not reach legacy PHP pages. Systemic scope: The same `` unescaped output pattern exists in at least 16 legacy PHP files across `core` and `plugins`, all involving the `description` (or equivalent `descr`) field: Core (8 locations): File | Description output --- | --- `firewall_rules_edit.php:1318,1400,1412` | Firewall rule edit — shaper dropdown `firewall_nat_out_edit.php:830` | Outbound NAT edit `firewall_schedule_edit.php:727` | Firewall schedule edit `firewall_scrub_edit.php:542` | Scrub rule edit `interfaces.php:1704` | Interface configuration `interfaces_ppps_edit.php:518` | PPP edit `interfaces_wireless_edit.php:167` | Wireless edit `system_gateway_groups_edit.php:262` | Gateway group edit Legacy plugins (8 locations): File | Plugin --- | --- `services_dhcp_edit.php:371` | ISC DHCPv4 `services_dhcp.php:653` | ISC DHCPv4 pool `services_dhcpv6_edit.php:248` | ISC DHCPv6 `services_rfc2136_edit.php:251` | RFC 2136 DDNS `services_igmpproxy_edit.php:175` | IGMP Proxy `vpn_openvpn_client.php:564` | OpenVPN Legacy Client `vpn_ipsec_phase1.php:775` | StrongSwan Legacy Phase 1 `vpn_ipsec_phase2.php:576` | StrongSwan Legacy Phase 2 #### PoC 1. Log in to OPNsense as an administrator. 2. Navigate to Firewall → Shaper → Pipes. 3. Click Create Pipe (the "+" button). 4. In the Description field, enter: ` ` 5. Click Save, then Apply. 6. Any administrator (including the attacker) who subsequently opens Firewall → Rules → Edit (any rule) will trigger the XSS: the malicious `description` is rendered unescaped in the shaper dropdown, causing `alert('XSS_PIPE')` to execute. The vulnerability has been confirmed via Playwright automation on OPNsense 25.x with `alert('XSS_PIPE')` triggering reliably when opening `firewall_rules_edit.php`. #### Impact * Type: Authenticated stored cross-site scripting (CWE-79). * Severity: High. * Affected users: All administrators who access Firewall Rules after an attacker has stored a malicious TrafficShaper description. The payload executes in the victim's browser with full access to session cookies, CSRF tokens, and the ability to perform arbitrary actions on behalf of the victim. * Attack surface: The underlying pattern — unescaped `` output in legacy PHP pages — means any description/descr field writable through MVC forms and readable through legacy PHP pages is potentially exploitable. The 16 locations listed above are the confirmed sinks; additional sinks may exist in other legacy PHP files. ### Severity High 8.1 # CVSS overall score This score calculates overall vulnerability severity from 0 to 10 and is based on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). / 10 #### CVSS v3 base metrics Attack vector Network Attack complexity Low Privileges required High User interaction ### CVE ID No known CVE ### Weaknesses Weakness CWE-79 #### Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users. LibreNMS is vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting (XSS) through multiple SNMP-sourced data fields that are rendered without HTML escaping in legacy PHP template pages. # Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Unescaped SNMP Data in Multiple Legacy Pages Moderate murrant published GHSA-v5jp-f342-234h Aug 4, 2026 ## Package librenms/librenms (Composer) ## Affected versions <= 26.2.0 ## Patched versions None ## Description # Security Advisory: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Unescaped SNMP Data in Multiple Legacy Pages ## Summary LibreNMS is vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting (XSS) through multiple SNMP-sourced data fields that are rendered without HTML escaping in legacy PHP template pages. An attacker with device management access (or network access to place a rogue SNMP device that gets enrolled) can inject crafted values that execute arbitrary JavaScript when any LibreNMS admin views the affected pages. The vulnerability was confirmed with data exfiltration of SNMP community strings and CSRF tokens from the admin's browser. ## Affected Product * Ecosystem: Composer * Package: `librenms/librenms` * Affected versions: <= 26.2.0 * Patched versions: None #### 4. ' - ' . trans_fb(...); if ($sla['tag']) { $name .= ': ' . $sla['tag']; } if ($sla['owner']) { $name .= ' (Owner: ' . $sla['owner'] . ')'; } echo "

$name

"; ### Root Cause All affected files are legacy PHP templates in `includes/html/pages/` that predate LibreNMS's migration to Laravel Blade templates. The modern Blade templates properly use `{{ }}` (auto-escaped) syntax, but these legacy pages use raw `echo` without `htmlspecialchars()` or `htmlentities()`. The data in all cases originates from SNMP polling of network devices and is stored in the database without sanitization. When rendered in the legacy pages, the SNMP-sourced values pass directly to the HTML output. ## Suggested Remediation Apply `htmlspecialchars()` to all SNMP-sourced data output in legacy PHP templates: // Before (vulnerable): echo '' . $peer['bgpPeerDescr'] . ""; // After (fixed): echo '' . htmlspecialchars($peer['bgpPeerDescr']) . ""; All affected locations requiring the same fix: File | Line | Field --- | --- | --- `includes/html/pages/routing/bgp.inc.php` | 329 | `$peer['bgpPeerDescr']` `includes/html/pages/device/routing/bgp.inc.php` | 241 | `$peer['bgpPeerDescr']` `includes/html/pages/device/routing/bgp.inc.php` | 230 | `$peer['bgpPeerLastErrorText']` `includes/html/pages/routing/vrf.inc.php` | 115 | `$vrf['vrf_name']` `includes/html/pages/routing/vrf.inc.php` | 116 | `$vrf['mplsVpnVrfDescription']` `includes/html/pages/routing/vrf.inc.php` | 117 | `$vrf['mplsVpnVrfRouteDistinguisher']` `includes/html/pages/device/processes.inc.php` | 88 | `$entry['user']` `includes/html/pages/device/processes.inc.php` | 89 | `$entry['command']` `includes/html/pages/device/slas.inc.php` | 20 | `$sla['tag']`, `$sla['owner']` Additionally, a broader audit of all legacy PHP templates in `includes/html/pages/` is recommended, as additional unescaped SNMP-sourced fields may exist beyond those identified here. ## Timeline * 2026-03-15: Vulnerability discovered and PoC confirmed on LibreNMS 26.2.0 (Docker) * 2026-03-15: Vendor notified via GitHub Security Advisory * 2026-03-20: Updated GitHub Security Advisory ## Credits * Discovered by: Dimas Herjunodarpito Notoprayitno (@dimashn04) ### Severity Moderate 5.8 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Security Advisories · smarty-php/smarty · GitHub (https://github.com/smarty-php/smarty/security/advisories) 【turn521529search3】 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last month; # Security: smarty-php/smarty ... ## Security Advisories ... * Cross site scripting vulnerability in Javascript escaping smarty-php / smarty Public * ### Uh oh! Crawled: last week; # Stored XSS in WebProfiler CodeExtension::fileExcerpt(): Unescaped Non-PHP File Rendering ... #### Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') # Stored XSS in WebProfiler CodeExtension::fileExcerpt(): Unescaped Non-PHP File Rendering Low nicolas-grekas published GHSA-hmr5-2xcr-v8pp May 20, 2026 ## Package symfony/symfony (Composer) ## Affected versions >=6.4.24, <6.4.40 >=7.2.9, <7.4.12 >=8, <8.0.12 ## Patched versions 6.4.40 7.4.12 8.0.12 symfony/twig-bridge (Composer) >=6.4.24, <6.4.40 6.4.40 symfony/web-profiler-bundle (Composer) >=7.2.9, <7.4.12 >=8, <8.0.12 7.4.12 8.0.12 ## Description ### Description Symfony's profiler, a development only debug UI, renders source-code excerpts on several pages using Twig's custom `file_excerpt` filter. This filter renders PHP files via `highlight_string()` (which escapes HTML), but renders non-PHP files by splitting on `\n` and interpolating each line directly into `{$line}` with no escaping. An attacker who can write arbitrary bytes into any file under the project root (including e.g. `var/log/dev.log`), achieves stored XSS against any developer who later opens that file in the profiler. ### Resolution The `file_excerpt` filter now properly escapes each line of non-PHP files using `htmlspecialchars()` before concatenating them. The patch for this issue is available here for branch 6.4. ### Credits We would like to thank Claude Mythos Preview (via Project Glasswing) for reporting the issue and providing the fix. ### Severity Low ### CVE ID CVE-2026-45072 ### Weaknesses Weakness CWE-79 #### Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users. The first one is in `packages/web/lib/fog/fogpage.class.php` below. ` private function _replaceNeeds($data) { ... foreach ((array)$arrayReplace as $name => &$val) { $this->dataFind[] = sprintf( '${%s}', $name ); $val = trim($val); $this->dataReplace[] = $val; // Here no HTML escaping to filter out high-risk HTML entities (e.g., " # Reflected XSS via unsanitized `lang` cookie error message on public authentication pages in Piwigo 16.3.0 Moderate plegall published GHSA-rr39-mf4j-6594 Jul 18, 2026 ## Package Piwigo/Piwigo ## Affected versions =16.3.0 ## Patched versions None ## Description ### Summary Piwigo 16.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting issue on the public pages `identification.php`, `register.php`, and `password.php`. These pages read the user-controlled `lang` cookie and, when the value is invalid, pass it into `fatal_error()`. The error renderer then embeds the cookie value directly into the HTML response without output encoding. As a result, attacker-controlled HTML/JavaScript such as `` is reflected into the response body. This is a real reflected XSS issue, but it is cookie-based rather than URL-only: exploitation requires the attacker to cause the victim browser to send a malicious `lang` cookie for the target origin.
